sources.citation: van der Wilden, Jaap & Jelly van der Wilden. 1975. Kemtuk phonology. Irian: Bulletin of Irian Jaya Development 4(3): 31-60 (papuaweb scan, scanned)
sources.tag: read: notes on stress
sources.note: SISTER language Kemtuk (kemt1242), not Mlap. Kwansu appears only in the 1975 SIL cognate table (Kemtuk-Kwansu 60%). Kemtuk stress p. 32: phonological words 'are of two general contrastive classes: ultimate stress and penultimate stress'. Not transferable to Mlap.

sources.citation: Voorhoeve, C.L. 1975. The Nimboran sub-phylum-level family. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study vol. 1, pp. 421-422. Pacific Linguistics C-38
sources.tag: read: notes on stress
sources.note: p. 421: Kwansu 'on the northern bank of the Ngremi, north of Gresik'; for the languages other than Nimboran 'the only data at hand are wordlists of Anceaux' collection'. The remark 'The language is non-tonal; stress is phonemic' (p. 422) refers to Nimboran only.

sources.citation: Anceaux, J.C. 1965. The Nimboran Language: Phonology and Morphology. VKI 44. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff (OAPEN scan)
sources.tag: read: silent on stress
sources.note: Kwansu-Bonggrang named only in the introduction (pp. 1-2) as a separate language whose position is 'half way between' Gresi/Kamtuk and Nimboran. Ch. VII 'The accent' (pp. 36-39) describes NIMBORAN only (place of accent lexically unpredictable). Nothing on Kwansu stress.
